questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Force Acting on a Body Given Its Velocity
questions.worked_solution:
By Newton’s second law,

$$
F(t)=ma(t),
$$

where $F(t)$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a(t)$ is the acceleration.

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({t}^{2}+3)) \\  & =\frac{2t}{{t}^{2}+3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =ma(t) \\  & =1\cdot \frac{2t}{{t}^{2}+3} \\  & =\frac{2t}{{t}^{2}+3}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

A body of mass $8\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons $(\text{N}).$

Calculate the magnitude of the force at time $t=4$ seconds.
questions.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\sqrt{t}-5\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-3)) \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{t}}-\frac{5}{t-3}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the acceleration at $t=4\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{4}}-\frac{5}{4-3} \\  & =1-5 \\  & =-4\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =8\cdot (-4) \\  & =-32.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of the force is

$$
|F|=|-32|=32\,\text{N}.
$$

According to Newton’s second law,

$$
F(t)=ma(t),
$$

where $F(t)$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a(t)$ is the acceleration.

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{e}^{\frac{t}{2}}) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{\frac{t}{2}}) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{2}{e}^{\frac{t}{2}} \\  & =2{e}^{\frac{t}{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the acceleration at $t=2\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}a(2\operatorname{ln}⁡3) & =2{e}^{\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}} \\  & =2{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =2(3) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}F(2\operatorname{ln}⁡3) & =ma(2\operatorname{ln}⁡3) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot 6 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of the force is

$$
|F(2\operatorname{ln}⁡3)|=|1|=1\,\text{N}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Force Acting on a Body Given Its Displacement
questions.worked_solution:
By Newton’s second law,

$$
F(t)=ma(t),
$$

where $F(t)$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a(t)$ is the acceleration.

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =ma(t) \\  & =1\cdot (2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining Moments When a Force Has Zero Magnitude
questions.problem:
A body of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t\ge 0$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t)=2{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-36t+2$ meters per second.
Calculate the time at which the force acting on the body has zero magnitude.
questions.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration. 

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-36t+2) \\  & =6{t}^{2}-6t-36\end{aligned}
$$

Since the mass is always positive, the force has zero magnitude when the acceleration equals zero. So, we set $a(t)=0$ and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6{t}^{2}-6t-36 & =0 \\ {t}^{2}-t-6 & =0 \\ (t-3)(t+2) & =0 \\ t & =-2,\,3\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\ge 0,$ we disregard the negative solution. 

Therefore, the force has zero magnitude at $t=3\,\text{s}.$

$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Determining Moments When a Force Has Zero Magnitude
canonical_examples.problem:
A body of mass $2 \, \textrm{kg}$ moves in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t\geq 0$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t) =2t^3-12t^2-30t+5$ meters per second.
Calculate the time when the force acting on the body has a magnitude of zero.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration. 

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}-12{t}^{2}-30t+5) \\  & =6{t}^{2}-24t-30\end{aligned}
$$

Since the mass is always positive, the force has zero magnitude when the acceleration equals zero. So, we set $a(t)=0$ and solve for $t{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}6{t}^{2}-24t-30 & =0 \\ {t}^{2}-4t-5 & =0 \\ (t+1)(t-5) & =0 \\ t & =-1,\,5\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t \geq 0,$ we disregard the negative solution. 

Therefore, the force has zero magnitude when $t=5 \, \textrm{s}.$
